question.text: The Finance Act 2025 amended Section 2(14) of the ITA. What is the implication of this amendment for the long-standing 'business income vs capital gains' controversy in Cat I/II AIFs?

answer.text: It repealed pass-through status entirely — all AIF income is now business income.

Securities dealt with by SEBI / IFSC Authority registered Cat I/II AIFs are DEEMED capital assets; consequently, any gain on transfer is taxed under 'Capital Gains', not 'Business Income', from FY 2025-26 onwards.
It made all AIF income exempt from tax.
It moved the taxation of AIFs from Section 115UB to Section 115BBH (crypto rules).

explanation.text: The Logic: The Finance Act 2025 amended Section 2(14) (definition of 'capital asset') to specifically include securities dealt with by SEBI / IFSC-Authority registered Cat I/II AIFs. From the financial year commencing 1 April 2025, any gain on transfer of such securities is taxed under the head 'Capital Gains' — closing the longstanding controversy over whether active securities trading by a Cat I/II AIF amounted to a 'business'. Consequently the Section 10(23FBB) MMR-at-fund-level exposure for securities gains largely disappears. The Trap: Option A inverts the direction of the reform. Option C invents a blanket exemption. Option D misroutes the change to the cryptocurrency section (Sec 115BBH), which is unrelated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the FA 2025 amendment. XIX-A updates distributor tax FAQs. XV/XXI-B do not cover this specifically. The amendment operates prospectively; pre-1-April-2025 years remain governed by the old facts-and-circumstances jurisprudence. Manager's Pro-Tip: Post-FA 2025, update your PPM taxation section to reflect that securities gains flow as CAPITAL GAINS with pass-through. LPs previously worried about fund-level MMR on 'trading income' can be reassured. Retain the facts-and-circumstances language for FY 2024-25 and earlier exits still in assessment.
